full_text: Intro 10 Mortgage CRM Functionalities That Simplify The Lending Process Home » 10 Mortgage CRM Functionalities That Simplify The Lending Process Finding just one mortgage lead can be costly. The cost of errors made when managing leads can add up very quickly. Reaching your goals with leads isn’t only about getting them, it will also depend on what happens after they enter your pipeline. Using a mortgage CRM software solves this problem by focusing on how the mortgage industry works. It provides tools and systems to help manage relationships with borrowers, adhere to regulations, and keep deals moving forward even when something has been missed. The first step in implementing a mortgage CRM is bringing together all your information, communications, and processes into one system. This way, every loan officer will always know where they stand within the pipeline and what they need to do next for each of their loans. In this blog, we have described the ten most important Mortgage CRM functionalities from the viewpoint of enhancing efficiency and profitability for mortgage companies. It also focuses on improved automation, better relationships with partners, and much more. What is a Mortgage CRM? A mortgage CRM enables the merging of data about borrowers into one single location. It automates any communication that follows after an application is filled out, tracking the loan from submission to completion, as well as keeping track of compliance aspects. How does CRM simplify the mortgage lending process? A mortgage CRM makes lending easier because it automates repetitive processes. The ability to keep all borrower information in one central location allows all members of the lending team to work from the same playbook and know exactly where every loan application is within the lending process. It eventually results in fewer errors, delays and missed opportunities throughout the entire pipeline. How does mortgage CRM improve borrower experience? A mortgage CRM improves borrowers’ experiences by keeping them in the loop every step of the way through text message (SMS) or e-mail. Borrowers will receive timely, helpful reminders that will enable them to complete their loan documents electronically (eSigning). Providing automated notifications allows the borrower to trust the loan officer, minimizes barriers, and converts happy borrowers into repeat customers and sources of ready-to-go referrals for business. 10 Best Mortgage CRM Functionalities 1. Lead Capture & Management Automation In mortgage lending, time is of great importance when contacting leads. Studies have shown leads which receive contact within a few minutes are much more likely to convert than leads contacted one hour after the original inquiry. However, many mortgage teams still use manual processes to follow up. Ultimately, this can create a costly delay in contacting their leads. In addition, some CRMs for mortgage lenders contain features that capture all of your leads automatically from all sources of inbound inquiries. For example, Zillow, LendingTree, your own website’s or any paid advertising you may be using. As soon as a lead is captured in an automated CRM, it can be quickly evaluated against a specified scoring criterion and sent to the appropriate loan officer based on location, type of product or workload. After lead qualification, automated sequences will continue in a mortgage lead management CRM. For example, if a borrower downloads a guide for first-time homebuyers, they will utilize a customized email and SMS drip campaign that will teach them about the pre-approval process. If they requested a rate quote but didn’t schedule a call, there would be an automated follow-up within an hour. Practitioner Tip: A loan officer that is spending two hours per day doing manual follow-up, could save over 40 hours each month by moving to automated workflows for their leads. This time can be spent making referral relationships and following up on existing loans. 2. LOS Integration (Loan Origination System Sync) A mortgage CRM cannot function on its own. It must communicate with the LOS. The LOS is where loans are processed. This involves underwriting, documentation and checking the compliance of a loan application. A mortgage CRM manages relationships with borrowers. If there is no real-time integration between the CRM and LOS, your team must enter information into both systems manually. The result is errors in processing and compliance because of manual data entry into two systems. Many of the major LOS platforms such as Encompass by ICE Mortgage Technology and Calyx Point have native integrations and/or API integrations with the major mortgage CRM platforms. When these systems are connected, they transfer important data back and forth automatically. Example: Once a loan officer updates a borrower’s contact information in their mortgage CRM, the loan officer’s action automatically updates the same contact information in the LOS. Example: When the underwriting team changes a loan from “conditionally approved” to “approved” by changing the loan’s status in the LOS, the LOS automatically triggers an email to send confirmation of this action to the borrower. This removes the need for duplicate data entry on form 1003. It ensures that each communication with the borrower seamlessly showcases the existing status of their loan. Why it matters: Duplicate data entry wastes time and also creates inconsistencies. Thus, it can lead to compliance failures and create confusion for the borrower at critical decision points. 3. Automated Compliance Management Mortgage lenders face one of the most highly scrutinized regulatory environments. At any given moment, loan officers and staff have to be compliant with RESPA, TRID, FHA guidelines, and the ongoing supervision of the CFPB. A mortgage CRM that includes integrated compliance management does much more than just store documents. It actively enforces compliance rules. Moreover, it automatically tracks when disclosures will need to be sent out, including sending notifications when deadlines are approaching. The system will flag documentation that is missing so that compliance issues. All borrower interactions with the lender (emails, telephone calls, changes in the status of loans) will be captured in an audit trail that remains unchanged. Role-based access controls provide another level of security. Loan processors only have access to information they require. Underwriters are only able to see information that is necessary to perform their underwriting functions. The front-line marketing workforce do not have access to sensitive financial information relevant to the borrower. Risk Callout: Non-compliance to RESPA can lead to severe penalties. So, when you have a CRM, you can have compliance alerts that will act as a protective measure. 4. Pipeline Tracking & Loan Status Visibility Mortgage CRMs have the ability to monitor the pipeline. It creates a dashboard view of each active loan at various status levels (loan application received → processing → appraisal ordered → Underwriting → Conditional Approval → Clear to Close → Funded). This view allows the Loan Officer to see all their loans in one place, while the Branch Manager can see all the loans in their Office. The biggest advantage a lender can have is allowing their customers visibility into what’s happening with their loans. By automating SMS and email updates based on the change in the status of their loans, lenders greatly reduce the number of phone calls to ask, “Where is my loan?.” Customers who receive proactive and timely updates about the progress of their mortgage loans are satisfied. They provide positive feedback, referrals and five-star ratings after their closing. 5. Document Management & eSignature One home purchase loan could have 300-500+ pages of documents that include funding disclosures, income verification, bank statements, appraisal reports, and title documents for the purchaser. If you try to manually track all these documents via emails or shared drives, it will upset borrowers because of the challenges it brings. One of the Mortgage CRM features is that it stores all of the documents in a single, secure and cloud-based location. It has automatic version control and deduplication capabilities. When a new appraisal is uploaded, the old appraisal is automatically archived. The team members can review it after getting the notifications regarding the updated version of the appraisal. Borrowers can electronically sign initial loan disclosures, intent-to-proceed forms, and complete their entire loan package using eSignature integration with DocuSign or Adobe Sign. This means that borrowers can complete all documents without having to visit a branch location. For example, a borrower may download, review their loan disclosures and return signed documents within ten minutes using their mobiles. Requests for documentation during the various phases of your loan are automated by your CRM at each phase. The request for your outstanding documentation is sent from your CRM either by email or text message as soon as your loan moves from the processing phase to the underwriting stage. 6. Marketing Automation & Drip Campaigns Most mortgage professionals know they have to “stay connected”. But they do not do that without a CRM that drives those communications. As a result, loan originators get busy, pipeline grows, and past clients drift away to competitors. Mortgage CRM marketing automation solves this problem by using pre-built, mortgage-specific drip campaigns. New leads in the first-time home buyer space will receive guidance/support via email about their credit scores, down payments, and the pre-approval process for six weeks. Borrowers who locked a rate will get notifications as their rate lock period closes in. The borrower will also receive an anniversary campaign, at the 2-year, 3-year, and 5-year anniversaries of their loans. It comes with personalized refinancing options. CRM for loan officers let lenders segment their audience based on loan type (FHA, VA, conventional, and jumbo loans), credit score, geography, lifecycle stage, and referring agent. This level of personalization creates higher open and conversion rates than sending out generic bulk emails. Tip: Targeting former borrowers with refinance opportunities turns out to be beneficial and yields highest ROI. 7. Referral Partner Management One of the most crucial functions for the long-term growth of your mortgage business is to effectively manage your referral partner network. Referral relationships with mortgage brokers, builders, financial advisors, and accountants account for a large amount of mortgage volume. In addition, referral leads convert at a much higher percentage than paid digital leads. To ease this, a referral partner management-focused mortgage CRM system will provide detailed profiles for each of their referral partners. It also consists of production history, preferred communication style, current listings, and the loan officers with whom they work. Your real estate partners will stay connected to you through your CRM as they receive automatic updates every week. In addition, your CRM will automatically generate ready-made marketing materials (such as flyers, email templates and social media posts) using branding. The result: Real estate agents keep sending their buyers to your loan officers because the experience is perfect, clear, and professional. 8. Mobile Access & Remote Workflow Support Loan officers generally aren’t sitting at a desk when they close loans. Instead, they close loans while attending an open house, client dinner or real-estate office, or a community event. Therefore, they are in need of full-service CRM irrespective of their location. A mobile app developed specifically for mortgages provides new lead and loan status notifications, one-tap calling with time-stamped logs of the phone call, and the ability to upload documents from the device’s camera to the system. The loan officer can respond to the underwriter’s request for a borrower’s letter of explanation and complete the update to the file in less than 2 minutes. The mobile app also gives loan officers the ability to go offline. This enables them to record notes, review borrower details, and line up actions that are performed automatically after the availability of the internet. Tip: When evaluating mobile CRM features, make sure that all testing occurs on the native application and not just via a desktop. A true mobile-first solution adjusts working in the field in real time. 9. Reporting, Analytics & AI-Powered Insights At the analytics level, the best platforms have predictive intelligence. By considering a borrower’s original loan terms, current market rates, and how long it’s been since they took out their first mortgage, the CRM can generate a list of past customers who are likely to refinance in the next 90 days. A loan officer who calls a customer with a personalized refinance offer has a much better chance of closing the loan than one who waits for a customer to respond to a competitor’s marketing material and calls back. AI-enabled prompts take the CRM lending process even further by suggesting what kind of contact should take place with each customer, on a daily basis. It is based on where they are in the process of their loan and what historical data tells them. This is the feature of CRM for loan officers that differentiates between successful and unsuccessful mortgage companies. The mortgage CRM reports conversion rates, average time from application to close for both loan types and individual loan officers, pull-through rates for applications, and overall performance rankings for each of the referral partners. Using these KPIs, managers can train loan originators that are producing at less than maximum capacity and provide feedback on which lead source is performing best. Competitive reality: Top mortgage teams are using AI-driven CRM systems to identify refinance opportunities and connect with them before their competitors can. 10. Scalability & Third-Party Integrations A mortgage CRM that works for one loan officer may not be appropriate for large multi-branch lenders. It’ll ultimately only cost you more money and time to switch to something else in the growth phase. When you look for a mortgage lending software, you want one that can grow with you. It should allow you to scale with your user base, handle large data, and handle more complex workflows without impacting performance. Moreover, you also want a pricing model that remains affordable even if your team grows. In addition to integrating with your LOS, an effective mortgage CRM should also perfectly integrate with all the other technology such as: Product Pricing Engines (PPE) offer real-time rates Point-of-Sale Systems (POS) provide borrower facing applications such as Blend or SimpleNexus Access to all three major credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian and TransUnion) to perform soft pull credit checks Accounting platforms to track commissions It is critical that you have Open API access if you run a large operation with custom-built workflow tools. If Open API access is not available, CRM will eventually work as a silo. Tip: Clarify what LOS, PPE and POS systems your new CRM integrates with and what will require middleware (like Zapier) before you sign an agreement. Native integrations are faster, more reliable and are less prone to breakage during platform upgrades. This way, every loan officer will always know where they stand within the pipeline and what they need to do next for each of their loans. In this blog, we have described the ten most important Mortgage CRM functionalities from the viewpoint of enhancing efficiency and profitability for mortgage companies. It also focuses on improved automation, better relationships with partners, and much more. What is a Mortgage CRM? A mortgage CRM enables the merging of data about borrowers into one single location. It automates any communication that follows after an application is filled out, tracking the loan from submission to completion, as well as keeping track of compliance aspects. How does CRM simplify the mortgage lending process? A mortgage CRM makes lending easier because it automates repetitive processes. The ability to keep all borrower information in one central location allows all members of the lending team to work from the same playbook and know exactly where every loan application is within the lending process. It eventually results in fewer errors, delays and missed opportunities throughout the entire pipeline. How does mortgage CRM improve borrower experience? A mortgage CRM improves borrowers’ experiences by keeping them in the loop every step of the way through text message (SMS) or e-mail. Borrowers will receive timely, helpful reminders that will enable them to complete their loan documents electronically (eSigning). Providing automated notifications allows the borrower to trust the loan officer, minimizes barriers, and converts happy borrowers into repeat customers and sources of ready-to-go referrals for business. 10 Best Mortgage CRM Functionalities 1. Lead Capture & Management Automation In mortgage lending, time is of great importance when contacting leads. Studies have shown leads which receive contact within a few minutes are much more likely to convert than leads contacted one hour after the original inquiry. However, many mortgage teams still use manual processes to follow up. Ultimately, this can create a costly delay in contacting their leads. In addition, some CRMs for mortgage lenders contain features that capture all of your leads automatically from all sources of inbound inquiries. For example, Zillow, LendingTree, your own website’s or any paid advertising you may be using. As soon as a lead is captured in an automated CRM, it can be quickly evaluated against a specified scoring criterion and sent to the appropriate loan officer based on location, type of product or workload. After lead qualification, automated sequences will continue in a mortgage lead management CRM. For example, if a borrower downloads a guide for first-time homebuyers, they will utilize a customized email and SMS drip campaign that will teach them about the pre-approval process. If they requested a rate quote but didn’t schedule a call, there would be an automated follow-up within an hour. Practitioner Tip: A loan officer that is spending two hours per day doing manual follow-up, could save over 40 hours each month by moving to automated workflows for their leads. This time can be spent making referral relationships and following up on existing loans. 2. LOS Integration (Loan Origination System Sync) A mortgage CRM cannot function on its own. It must communicate with the LOS. The LOS is where loans are processed. This involves underwriting, documentation and checking the compliance of a loan application. A mortgage CRM manages relationships with borrowers. If there is no real-time integration between the CRM and LOS, your team must enter information into both systems manually. The result is errors in processing and compliance because of manual data entry into two systems. Many of the major LOS platforms such as Encompass by ICE Mortgage Technology and Calyx Point have native integrations and/or API integrations with the major mortgage CRM platforms. When these systems are connected, they transfer important data back and forth automatically. Example: Once a loan officer updates a borrower’s contact information in their mortgage CRM, the loan officer’s action automatically updates the same contact information in the LOS. Example: When the underwriting team changes a loan from “conditionally approved” to “approved” by changing the loan’s status in the LOS, the LOS automatically triggers an email to send confirmation of this action to the borrower. This removes the need for duplicate data entry on form 1003. It ensures that each communication with the borrower seamlessly showcases the existing status of their loan. Why it matters: Duplicate data entry wastes time and also creates inconsistencies. Thus, it can lead to compliance failures and create confusion for the borrower at critical decision points. 3. Automated Compliance Management Mortgage lenders face one of the most highly scrutinized regulatory environments. At any given moment, loan officers and staff have to be compliant with RESPA, TRID, FHA guidelines, and the ongoing supervision of the CFPB. A mortgage CRM that includes integrated compliance management does much more than just store documents. It actively enforces compliance rules. Moreover, it automatically tracks when disclosures will need to be sent out, including sending notifications when deadlines are approaching. The system will flag documentation that is missing so that compliance issues. All borrower interactions with the lender (emails, telephone calls, changes in the status of loans) will be captured in an audit trail that remains unchanged. Role-based access controls provide another level of security. Loan processors only have access to information they require. Underwriters are only able to see information that is necessary to perform their underwriting functions. The front-line marketing workforce do not have access to sensitive financial information relevant to the borrower. Risk Callout: Non-compliance to RESPA can lead to severe penalties. So, when you have a CRM, you can have compliance alerts that will act as a protective measure. 4. Pipeline Tracking & Loan Status Visibility Mortgage CRMs have the ability to monitor the pipeline. It creates a dashboard view of each active loan at various status levels (loan application received → processing → appraisal ordered → Underwriting → Conditional Approval → Clear to Close → Funded). This view allows the Loan Officer to see all their loans in one place, while the Branch Manager can see all the loans in their Office. The biggest advantage a lender can have is allowing their customers visibility into what’s happening with their loans. By automating SMS and email updates based on the change in the status of their loans, lenders greatly reduce the number of phone calls to ask, “Where is my loan?.” Customers who receive proactive and timely updates about the progress of their mortgage loans are satisfied. They provide positive feedback, referrals and five-star ratings after their closing. 5. Document Management & eSignature One home purchase loan could have 300-500+ pages of documents that include funding disclosures, income verification, bank statements, appraisal reports, and title documents for the purchaser. If you try to manually track all these documents via emails or shared drives, it will upset borrowers because of the challenges it brings. One of the Mortgage CRM features is that it stores all of the documents in a single, secure and cloud-based location. It has automatic version control and deduplication capabilities. When a new appraisal is uploaded, the old appraisal is automatically archived. The team members can review it after getting the notifications regarding the updated version of the appraisal. Borrowers can electronically sign initial loan disclosures, intent-to-proceed forms, and complete their entire loan package using eSignature integration with DocuSign or Adobe Sign. This means that borrowers can complete all documents without having to visit a branch location. For example, a borrower may download, review their loan disclosures and return signed documents within ten minutes using their mobiles. Requests for documentation during the various phases of your loan are automated by your CRM at each phase. The request for your outstanding documentation is sent from your CRM either by email or text message as soon as your loan moves from the processing phase to the underwriting stage. 6. Marketing Automation & Drip Campaigns Most mortgage professionals know they have to “stay connected”. But they do not do that without a CRM that drives those communications. As a result, loan originators get busy, pipeline grows, and past clients drift away to competitors. Mortgage CRM marketing automation solves this problem by using pre-built, mortgage-specific drip campaigns. New leads in the first-time home buyer space will receive guidance/support via email about their credit scores, down payments, and the pre-approval process for six weeks. Borrowers who locked a rate will get notifications as their rate lock period closes in. The borrower will also receive an anniversary campaign, at the 2-year, 3-year, and 5-year anniversaries of their loans. It comes with personalized refinancing options. CRM for loan officers let lenders segment their audience based on loan type (FHA, VA, conventional, and jumbo loans), credit score, geography, lifecycle stage, and referring agent. This level of personalization creates higher open and conversion rates than sending out generic bulk emails. Tip: Targeting former borrowers with refinance opportunities turns out to be beneficial and yields highest ROI. 7. Referral Partner Management One of the most crucial functions for the long-term growth of your mortgage business is to effectively manage your referral partner network. Referral relationships with mortgage brokers, builders, financial advisors, and accountants account for a large amount of mortgage volume. In addition, referral leads convert at a much higher percentage than paid digital leads. To ease this, a referral partner management-focused mortgage CRM system will provide detailed profiles for each of their referral partners. It also consists of production history, preferred communication style, current listings, and the loan officers with whom they work. Your real estate partners will stay connected to you through your CRM as they receive automatic updates every week. In addition, your CRM will automatically generate ready-made marketing materials (such as flyers, email templates and social media posts) using branding. The result: Real estate agents keep sending their buyers to your loan officers because the experience is perfect, clear, and professional. 8. Mobile Access & Remote Workflow Support Loan officers generally aren’t sitting at a desk when they close loans. Instead, they close loans while attending an open house, client dinner or real-estate office, or a community event. Therefore, they are in need of full-service CRM irrespective of their location. A mobile app developed specifically for mortgages provides new lead and loan status notifications, one-tap calling with time-stamped logs of the phone call, and the ability to upload documents from the device’s camera to the system. The loan officer can respond to the underwriter’s request for a borrower’s letter of explanation and complete the update to the file in less than 2 minutes. The mobile app also gives loan officers the ability to go offline. This enables them to record notes, review borrower details, and line up actions that are performed automatically after the availability of the internet. Tip: When evaluating mobile CRM features, make sure that all testing occurs on the native application and not just via a desktop. A true mobile-first solution adjusts working in the field in real time. 9. Reporting, Analytics & AI-Powered Insights At the analytics level, the best platforms have predictive intelligence. By considering a borrower’s original loan terms, current market rates, and how long it’s been since they took out their first mortgage, the CRM can generate a list of past customers who are likely to refinance in the next 90 days. A loan officer who calls a customer with a personalized refinance offer has a much better chance of closing the loan than one who waits for a customer to respond to a competitor’s marketing material and calls back. AI-enabled prompts take the CRM lending process even further by suggesting what kind of contact should take place with each customer, on a daily basis. It is based on where they are in the process of their loan and what historical data tells them. This is the feature of CRM for loan officers that differentiates between successful and unsuccessful mortgage companies. The mortgage CRM reports conversion rates, average time from application to close for both loan types and individual loan officers, pull-through rates for applications, and overall performance rankings for each of the referral partners. Using these KPIs, managers can train loan originators that are producing at less than maximum capacity and provide feedback on which lead source is performing best. Competitive reality: Top mortgage teams are using AI-driven CRM systems to identify refinance opportunities and connect with them before their competitors can. 10. Scalability & Third-Party Integrations A mortgage CRM that works for one loan officer may not be appropriate for large multi-branch lenders. It’ll ultimately only cost you more money and time to switch to something else in the growth phase. When you look for a mortgage lending software, you want one that can grow with you. It should allow you to scale with your user base, handle large data, and handle more complex workflows without impacting performance. Moreover, you also want a pricing model that remains affordable even if your team grows. In addition to integrating with your LOS, an effective mortgage CRM should also perfectly integrate with all the other technology such as: Product Pricing Engines (PPE) offer real-time rates Point-of-Sale Systems (POS) provide borrower facing applications such as Blend or SimpleNexus Access to all three major credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian and TransUnion) to perform soft pull credit checks Accounting platforms to track commissions It is critical that you have Open API access if you run a large operation with custom-built workflow tools. If Open API access is not available, CRM will eventually work as a silo. Tip: Clarify what LOS, PPE and POS systems your new CRM integrates with and what will require middleware (like Zapier) before you sign an agreement. Native integrations are faster, more reliable and are less prone to breakage during platform upgrades.
